messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int shield = 10;
if (shield < 0); fire();

Question: Does it fire?
The student answered: yes

The student understands this correctly: A `;` right after the if/for/while header is an empty body; the next statement is not part of it.

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["Since the semicolon ends the if part, fire() always runs no matter the shield value.", "The condition never actually controls anything because that semicolon sits between if and fire.", "After the if with semicolon, the next line just executes on its own.", "Because shield is 10 the if is true, but the semicolon makes the body empty and fire still runs.", "The fire call comes after the empty if statement, so it happens unconditionally."]}

sentences: Since the semicolon ends the if part, fire() always runs no matter the shield value.
The condition never actually controls anything because that semicolon sits between if and fire.
After the if with semicolon, the next line just executes on its own.
Because shield is 10 the if is true, but the semicolon makes the body empty and fire still runs.
The fire call comes after the empty if statement, so it happens unconditionally.
